authorization: 2026-10-20 user authorized the next experiments listed in roadmap section 4
question: Sequential-write damage lands on old facts that share the subject or relation with the written fact. Does protecting those address neighbours, instead of random old samples, keep new facts, double-new composition and old knowledge at the same time?

protection.teacher: native300k theta0 output distribution at answer and EOS positions, same as the original teachers
protection.neighbor_atoms: old graph atoms with the written subject (half) or the written relation (half); all from the relation pool when the subject has none
protection.neighbor_chains: phi7.2 trained chains whose first entity or bridge is the written subject (half), or whose first or second relation is the written relation (half)
protection.random_fill: mixed arms fill the remaining slots with the first rows of the original random teacher batch of the same step
protection.excluded: every row of the seven old evaluation pools and every mixed-query old companion
protection.sampling: per fact, deterministic from seed + fact index; without replacement until a pool is exhausted, then reshuffled

evaluation: identical read_state after every write and two-step reference at each stream end; summarized by summarize_streams and the address-grouped interference analysis
verification: per user preference: CPU contract tests and ruff only; no source freeze, hash manifest or separate CUDA preflight
